points: Q3 2026 is still live, so the October 30 print will reveal whether Virtu is tracking the 90-day revenue estimate lift of +13.6% and whether the 5-up/0-down analyst revision trend is justified by execution.
FY1 EPS of $7.30 embeds 27% growth, while FY2 EPS of $6.93 implies a 5% contraction; the print and any guidance will show whether FY1 is achievable or whether FY2 pressure is real.

The name trades at 9.2x FY1 earnings and a 0.33x PEG, roughly half the theme median on both metrics; the print will reveal whether that discount reflects a real fundamental gap or a valuation opportunity.
Peer prints from CBOE, ICE, MSCI and DFIN in late October will provide read-throughs on trading volumes and market-data demand ahead of Virtu's report; stronger results there support the long case.
Q2 2026 results are already public and showed revenue momentum; the Q3 print will reveal whether that momentum carried through the summer quarter.
Reports suggest buyback activity may have slowed; the Q3 print will clarify whether capital returns remain a tailwind for EPS or have become a headwind.
With the Financial Exchanges & Data theme active and breadth at +0.60, Virtu's guidance tone on market-making volumes, execution services and cost discipline will set the trade setup into year-end.
watch: Q3 revenue growth at or above the +13.6% 90-day estimate — supports the long.
FY1 EPS holding near $7.30 and FY2 EPS not revised lower — supports the long.
FY1 P/E staying at a discount to the theme median while fundamentals hold — supports the long.
Peer prints (CBOE, ICE, MSCI, DFIN) showing healthy volumes and data demand — supports the long.
